The **Japan Series Most Valuable Player (MVP) Award** (日本シリーズ最高殊勲選手, *Nippon Shirīzu Saikō Shukun Senshu*) is given to the player deemed to have the most impact on his team's performance in the [Japan Series](Japan_Series "Japan Series"), which is the final round of the [Nippon Professional Baseball](Nippon_Professional_Baseball "Nippon Professional Baseball") (NPB) postseason. The award was first presented in 1950.

The series follows a [best-of-seven playoff](Best-of-seven_playoff "Best-of-seven playoff") format and occurs after the two-stage [Climax Series](Climax_Series "Climax Series"). It is played by the winners of the [Central League](Central_League "Central League") Stage 2 series and the [Pacific League](Pacific_League "Pacific League") Stage 2 series.[[1]](Japan_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-1)

[Kaoru Betto](Kaoru_Betto "Kaoru Betto") won the inaugural award in 1950 with the [Mainichi Orions](Mainichi_Orions "Mainichi Orions"). Depending upon definitions, the first non-Japanese to win the award was either [Andy Miyamoto](Andy_Miyamoto "Andy Miyamoto") in 1961 or [Joe Stanka](Joe_Stanka "Joe Stanka") in 1964.[[2]](Japan_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-2) Fifteen Japan Series MVPs were inducted into the [Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame](Japanese_Baseball_Hall_of_Fame "Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame");[[3]](Japan_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-3) [Osamu Higashio](Osamu_Higashio "Osamu Higashio") (1982) is the only Hall of Famer to have won the Japan Series MVP between 1981 and 2000. Higashio is also the first and only [pitcher](Pitcher "Pitcher") to appear solely as a [reliever](Relief_pitcher "Relief pitcher") to win the Japan Series MVP. Eight of the ten Japan Series MVPs who have won the award since 2000 are still active in professional baseball—[Atsuya Furuta](Atsuya_Furuta "Atsuya Furuta") and [Takashi Ishii](Takashi_Ishii_(baseball) "Takashi Ishii (baseball)") are the Japan Series MVPs from that period who are inactive. [Hideki Matsui](Hideki_Matsui "Hideki Matsui") and [Norihiro Nakamura](Norihiro_Nakamura "Norihiro Nakamura") are they only two Japan Series MVPs to play in [Major League Baseball](Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball") (MLB). While Nakamura's MLB career lasted less than one season, Matsui's lasted seven seasons. He became the only player to be named both a Japan Series and a [World Series MVP](World_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "World Series Most Valuable Player Award") after winning the latter award in 2009.[[4]](Japan_Series_Most_Valuable_Player_Award#cite_note-4) The reigning Japan Series MVP is [Yutaro Sugimoto](Yutaro_Sugimoto "Yutaro Sugimoto") of the [Orix Buffaloes](Orix_Buffaloes "Orix Buffaloes").

Sixteen of the 60 Japan Series MVPs have also won the [NPB MVP](Nippon_Professional_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Nippon Professional Baseball Most Valuable Player Award") or the [Eiji Sawamura Award](Eiji_Sawamura_Award "Eiji Sawamura Award") in the same season. [Shigeru Sugishita](Shigeru_Sugishita "Shigeru Sugishita") (1954), [Tsuneo Horiuchi](Tsuneo_Horiuchi "Tsuneo Horiuchi") (1972) and [Takehiro Ishii](Takehiro_Ishii "Takehiro Ishii") (1992) are the only players to have won all three awards in the same season. Two players won the Eiji Sawamura Award and the Japan Series MVP in the same season: [Takehiko Bessho](Takehiko_Bessho "Takehiko Bessho") (1955) and [Takashi Nishimoto](Takashi_Nishimoto "Takashi Nishimoto") (1981).
